awd_titl_txt: Collaborative Research: Research Infrastructure: Shared Unified Research Fleet IT Support for the ARF, Pilot Project (SURF-IT)
awd_abstract_narration:
The University of Alaska, Fairbanks (UAF) in collaboration with the University of Washington (UW) and University of Rhode Island (URI) propose to pilot a Shared Unified Research Fleet IT Support (SURF-IT) program for the US Academic Research Fleet (ARF). SURF-IT aims to establish a Managed Service Provider (MSP) to deliver essential IT and cybersecurity support to the ARF. By leveraging shared resources among UAF, UW, and URI, SURF-IT proposes to provide cost-effective, centralized technical services. This initiative will enhance operational efficiency, ensure robust cyberinfrastructure, and address the gap in dedicated IT support within the ARF.

Oceanographic research vessels in the ARF provide at-sea laboratories that support scientists, engineers, post-doctoral scholars, graduate and undergraduate students as well as technicians and teachers as they pursue fundamental research in the marine environment. The principal impact of the present proposal is under Merit Review Criterion 2 of the Proposal Guidelines (NSF 23-525). It will provide fundamental support for cybersecurity and cyberinfrastructure to technicians, science, and crew for NSF-funded oceanographic research projects (which individually undergo separate review by the relevant research program of NSF).

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
1. Summary

The Shared Unified Research Fleet IT Support or SURF-IT was a pilot program to provide IT support and cyberinfrastructure services. SURF-IT provided resources and expertise, ensuring that all participating institutions have access to professional IT services. By supplying technical support on an opt-in basis, SURF-IT allows institutions to leverage a pool of shared resources, increasing operational efficiency and security without the need for each to maintain its own full-time IT personnel.

The SURF-IT program was a collaborative proposal between the University of Alaska Fairbanks (primary), the University of Rhode Island, and the University of Washington. A collaborative approach was chosen due to the IT expertise of the institutions and the expected workload of the program.

2. Services Provided

For the ARF members who participate, SURF-IT serves as a point of contact for IT issues and advanced support. SURF-IT specializes in services tailored to the unique needs of maritime research, including:

  • Virtual CI/CS Helpdesk: A dedicated helpdesk handles common IT issues for the ARF, ranging from connectivity problems to hardware or software troubleshooting. This service provides fast resolution for routine issues -especially for onboard marine technicians, reducing downtime for research activities, and maintaining a common knowledge base to be shared with all participants. For this pilot project the helpdesk was a common email address under the UNOLS domain.
  • Tier 2/3 Support and Vendor Liaison: For more complex issues, SURF-IT acts as a liaison with vendors and institutional partners, ensuring swift access to advanced technical resources.
  • FortiGate Firewall Support: The NSF FortiGate Firewall project started in CY2024 as a unified approach to addressing the increasing cybersecurity regulations in the maritime industry. The FortiGate firewalls also address long-running complaints from sailing scientists regarding the variability in user experience from vessel to vessel. SURF-IT jumped into the technical management role for the Fortigate project and accomplished the rollout to remaining ARF vessels through 2026.
  • Technical Assistance for CyberInfrastructure Projects (aka virtual Network Engineers and virtual Sysadmins): Cyberinfrastructure projects, such as the expertise that the member institutions lack (including on-site projects). SURF-IT designs network upgrades and suggests proper hardware which meets the needs of the vessels and the security requirements of regulatory bodies. SURF-IT coordinates installations and upgrades for vessels and trains technicians as needed with the skills required for these specialized tasks, minimizing disruption to ongoing research.

3. Project Engagements & Work Complete

Project Engagements:

 
A series of project meetings are held for each engagement with SURF-IT members joining the pre-planning discussion. Post install support is also offered to operators. These project summaries are heavily redacted for cybersecurity reasons.

RV Hugh Sharp

November 2025, On-site

SURF-IT technicians installed, configured, and tested two FortiGate firewalls in an HA pair. Existing shore and satellite internet infrastructure was reconfigured into WAN aggregation switches and the balancing and failover configurations were modified.

RV Atlantic Explorer

December 2025, Remote support

SURF-IT technicians provided remote support on a number of issues. Atlantic Explorer had reported numerous DNS issues since the initial FortiGate rollout which were resolved. The FortiGate firewalls were upgraded to the latest firmware and testing was performed satisfactorily. The BIOS team requested assistance with the synchronization of their backup infrastructure and technical wiki to shore facilities. The TimeZero navigation computers were isolated into a separate VLAN for security.

RV Marcus Langseth

January 2026, On-site

SURF-IT technicians installed, configured, and tested two FortiGate firewalls in an HA pair. A hardware FortiAnalyzer was installed to store security logs locally.

RV Pelican

March 2026, On-site

SURF-IT assisted the RV Pelican with CI infrastructure upgrades needed to migrate to the OpenRVDAS data acquisition system and Coriolix sensor management. Their sensor infrastructure relies heavily on point-to-point RS-232 serial connections. The SURF-IT team mapped the sensors and installed computing infrastructure to host the new software. Throughout the process, SURF-IT conducted a thorough CI/CS review and recommended needed upgrades.

SURF-IT also helped the RV Pelican migrate to the Glubus file transfer utility for sending data into the R2R national archives.

RV Blue Heron

April 2026, On-site

SURF-IT technicians installed, configured, and tested two FortiGate firewalls in an HA pair. Existing shore and satellite internet infrastructure was reconfigured into WAN aggregation switches and the balancing and failover configurations were modified. A local FortiAnalyzer hardware appliance was installed for log collection. Existing LAN infrastructure was renamed and reworked for compatibility with the FortiGate firewalls.

RV Sikuliaq

May 2026, On-site

SURF-IT technicians assisted the RV Sikuliaq with a large virtualization infrastructure migration from vCenter to Proxmox.
            

Community outreach surveys 

ARF vessels have been implementing competing virtualization technologies for the past decade. As ships begin to rely on this infrastructure, supporting the variety of implementations becomes a challenge. SURF-IT developed a Virtualization Survey which was sent to ARF vessels in November/December 2025. The results of which will be used for technical decision-making and future migrations.
